newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Moderate wage increases recommended for Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Moderate wage increases recommended for Singapore.

text.p: Wage increases in Singapore in 1997 should be moderate on account of slower economic and productivity growth, the National Wages Council (NWC) said on Friday.

"Employers and trade unions should take into account Singapore's slower economic and productivity growth," NWC chairman Lim Chong Yah told a news conference on the council's recommended wage increase guidelines.
The NWC said it expects a 1997 average wage increase of less than last year's 6.7 percent, when the economy grew by 7.0 percent.

"This year MTI (the Ministry of Trade and Industry) expects the economy to grow by 5 percent to 7 percent," Lim said. "NWC thus expects the average wage increase to be less than last year's 6.7 percent."
The NWC noted 1996 productivity growth was 0.7 percent, down from 3.6 percent in 1995.
A rise in the number of unprofitable companies in Singapore also was also taken into account in recommendations.
"In 1996, 21.9 percent of the companies in Singapore were unprofitable against 7.2 percent profitable companies," Lim said.

Other factors mentioned by the council included a decline in export growth, an increase in unit business costs, increased relative unit labour cost, a stable CPI, and intense global and regional competition.
